hero.label: Made for Certus AI
hero.headline: I want to bring Voice AI to every restaurant operator who needs it.
hero.subheadline: Certus AI is solving a real, unglamorous problem that costs restaurants money every single day: missed and mishandled phone calls. I want to be the person who gets operators to finally pick up the phone on that solution. Having already closed B2B clients in an AI-adjacent space and learned how to build conviction with skeptical buyers, I think this is exactly the right role at exactly the right moment for me.

whyCompany.title: Restaurants are a massive, underserved market for AI automation
whyCompany.body: Independent and chain restaurants take hundreds of calls a day for reservations, orders, and questions, yet almost none of them have touched AI voice tooling. That gap between the size of the problem and the current adoption rate is where great BDR opportunities live. Certus AI is positioned to own that gap before anyone else does.

whyCompany.title: Early BDR hire at a seed-stage AI company is a career-defining seat
whyCompany.body: Joining now means helping shape the outreach playbook, not just executing someone else's. The patterns Ignacio builds in these first months will define how Certus AI sells for years. That kind of ownership is exactly what he is looking for in a first full-time role.

whyCompany.title: His BDR track record translates directly to this motion
whyCompany.body: At Copygen.ai, Ignacio ran cold outreach and LinkedIn sequences through HubSpot and helped land 15 to 20 paying clients in an AI SaaS context, which is the same sell-a-new-technology-to-skeptical-operators challenge Certus AI faces. His time at NextAfter sharpened his instinct for message testing and conversion, skills that matter just as much when booking restaurant demos as when optimizing fundraising campaigns.

quote: Restaurants are one of the last business categories still losing real money to something as fixable as a missed phone call. I want to be the person knocking on those doors and showing operators there is a better way.
